description: Maya, who is keeping the family's box of old negatives and the only scanner available to them, must decide which images to digitize, how the files will be preserved, who may see them, and whether to add a narrated presentation for the family reunion.

agents.name: Maya
agents.role: Family Photo Archive Keeper and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: The family has one box of old photographic negatives and prints from several decades of family events.
shared_context.S2: Maya has the family's scanner, which can digitize exactly 12 images before the family reunion.
shared_context.S3: The family reunion is scheduled for 2026-09-05, and Maya is preparing a small photo presentation for it.
shared_context.S4: The family normally does a round-robin check before finalizing reunion plans so each person can raise a practical concern or offer help.
shared_context.S5: The digitized files will be kept with the physical photographs after the reunion.

PF1.text: Owen remembers that the family agreed photographs from their mother's hospital stay may be shared only among family members, not shown publicly or posted online; he has not raised the agreement with Maya.

PF2.text: Riley recently asked conservator Dana Brooks for advice, and Dana recommended scanning the negatives as 600 dpi TIFF files and storing the physical photographs in acid-free sleeves; this advice has not reached the group.

PF3.text: Tessa promised her grandfather that she would record a 15-minute narration about the family's 1978 camping trip if the reunion presentation included exactly four images from that trip; she has not told Maya about the promise.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly four of the digitized images must be from the 1978 camping trip.
The files must be saved as 600 dpi TIFF files.
The physical photographs must be placed in acid-free sleeves.
Images from the hospital stay must be restricted to family-only access.
The presentation must include the 15-minute narration.
A commitment to record the narration must exist.

decisive_facts.why: The family's hospital-stay agreement changes presentation access from ordinary reunion or public sharing to the exact family-only setting.
Dana Brooks's recommendation changes the file format to 600 dpi TIFF and the physical storage to acid-free sleeves.
Tessa's promise changes the selection to exactly four 1978 camping images, requires a narrated presentation, and creates the narration-recording commitment.
